acceptance: Evaluation recorded on this item: measured eligible savings for each option, and a go or keep-Trunk-unchanged decision (keep-unchanged is a valid result, for example if tree-equivalent medium reuse is rare or the nightly lane cannot replace the lost detection window)
Before any implementation: the measured eligible savings are recorded, the owner approves delayed Python 3.12 detection, and the replacement nightly lane is shown to execute successfully

Medium reuse condition, if pursued: reuse only successful, complete full-medium evidence bound to the actual checked-out PR merge tree (PR checkout defaults to the synthetic merge ref, not the feature head: ci.yml:859-863,995-1000), run and attempt, head and base, workflow and test configuration and lane set, where that tested tree equals the delivered squash tree (see docs/internal/repo-admin-settings.md:130-136). Missing, stale, failed, partial or ambiguous evidence runs the full tier.

If implemented: release admission rejects a wrong SHA, wrong event, wrong attempt and a failed latest run, and the intended repaired arm and revert behaviour is verified (not preservation of the earlier attribution bug, fixed in PR #3415)
Owner decision recorded: the savings target and its non-inferiority tolerance for PR CI queue time (the earlier fixed 'below 40 minutes' target is not adopted because it was an unsupported cliff)

If implemented: Trunk runner-minutes per merge are measured with the CI usage report over 7 days before and after (Trunk coverage counted separately), and PR CI job queue time median and p90 stay within the tolerance
Any coverage dropped from Trunk (for example Python 3.12 fast) is named with where it is still covered

description: Decide, with measurements, whether Trunk should be trimmed at all; keeping Trunk unchanged is an allowed and documented outcome. Sampled Trunk cost (40 job records) averages 49.39 runner-minutes per run: fast 9.37, medium collection plus four shards 26.03, correctness gates 7.01, required local cases 3.91, TPC-DS parity draws 2.39, distribution producer 0.67. Fast, medium and correctness are about 85.9% of that time, but that is not the share that can safely be removed: the Trunk tree differs from the PR tree, Trunk fast runs Python 3.12 where PR fast runs 3.14 (trunk.yml:33, ci.yml:867), and live selection already removes some corresponding PR coverage. Removing all fast work saves 9.37 minutes a merge (about five runner-hours a day at 32 merges a day) and leaves 40.02 minutes a run; reusing medium evidence would save about 26 minutes per eligible merge before lookup overhead. Trunk must stay per push: it is the only test of the merged tree, release admission needs the whole latest exact-SHA Trunk push run to succeed and its dist-artifact (scripts/release_artifact_consumer.py:188-230), and the arm gate names the culprit from Trunk runs. This item waits for cov-select-exit-shadow-20261021 to finish, which includes its 14-day observation window, not merely its flag-flip PR; Trunk coverage and tested lanes must not change inside that window. Two options to evaluate: (a) drop or thin the Python 3.12 fast lane, which is a distinct Python-version backstop (nightly.yml:31,69-71 still runs 3.12 fast, but Nightly Validation run 40083832625 failed, so its health must be shown); (b) skip the medium tier only when full-medium evidence from the PR run is bound to the tested tree (see acceptance). Measure how often option (b) would be eligible before building anything. The repository is public, so GitHub-hosted runner minutes are free; the binding limit is the concurrency cap. Queue time and PR time-to-green are the primary success metrics, runner-minutes secondary.
